title: TP Hang Repro Stress Suite (Spec): Traffic Patterns, Fault Injection, and CI/Perf-Canary Integration
author: Sahana Iyer
body:
## Overview
This document specifies the TP Hang Repro Stress Suite: a deterministic-ish harness for reproducing and detecting tensor-parallel (TP) hangs/timeouts under sustained load. The suite is designed to:

- Reproduce known hang signatures observed in production (comm stalls, kernel stalls, scheduler/barrier deadlocks, cancellation-induced deadlocks).
- Provide actionable pass/fail signals for CI and perf-canary that correlate with customer-visible symptoms (timeouts/5xx, “stuck” streams).
- Produce artifacts that make triage faster (rank-level progress, collective latency distributions, timeline markers for fault injection).

The suite is not intended to be a microbenchmark. It is a reliability-oriented stress runner with controlled variability, fault injection knobs, and explicit stall detection.

## Goals
1) Reproducibility across environments
- Same scenario config should reproduce (or at least strongly trend toward) the same failure mode on supported GPU types.
- Must be runnable locally (single node) and in the benchmark lab / perf-canary infrastructure.

2) Coverage of the most common hang triggers
- High concurrency + mixed sequence lengths + continuous batching.
- Long-running streaming responses with client disconnect/cancellation.
- Partial rank slowdown and collective jitter.
- Backpressure and scheduling fairness under overload.

3) Clear pass/fail criteria
- Detect forward-progress stalls at the TP-group and request levels.
- Disallow silent stalls (requests hang indefinitely without errors).
- Ensure failures are surfaced as explicit errors with reasons and metrics.

4) Operationally usable artifacts
- Scenario-run metadata (hardware, driver, runtime build, flags).
- Per-rank progress counters and collective latency histograms.
- Minimal logs required for immediate classification (comm stall vs kernel stall vs scheduler starvation).

## Non-goals
- Replacing full end-to-end model quality evals.
- Benchmarking absolute throughput leadership.
- Simulating customer-specific network driver failures (tracked separately; this suite focuses on runtime behavior and controllable faults).

## Terminology
- TP group: the set of ranks participating in a single tensor-parallel partition.
- Forward progress: tokens generated / decode steps completed per rank over time.
- Stall: forward progress halts for longer than the configured stall threshold while work remains outstanding.
- Fault injection: deliberate perturbation to trigger failure modes (rank delay, forced cancel, forced timeout, etc.).

## System under test (SUT)
The suite targets Redwood’s serving runtime TP execution path, including:
- Scheduler TP-group lifecycle and barrier/cancellation semantics.
- Kernel and collective execution (NCCL collectives, stream/event coordination).
- Watchdog + quarantine behavior at the TP-group level (where available).

The suite runs against a dedicated test endpoint (preferred) or a direct runtime process invocation (fallback for local repro).

## High-level architecture
### Components
1) Scenario runner (tp_stress_runner)
- Reads a scenario config (YAML/JSON) and orchestrates phases: warmup → stress → recovery/teardown.
- Drives client traffic (streaming and non-streaming).
- Applies fault injection according to a schedule.
- Collects artifacts and emits a final verdict.

2) Traffic generator
- Uses Redwood SDK-compatible HTTP client (to mimic real streaming behavior) OR a load harness used by perf-canary.
- Supports:
  - streaming token consumption with configurable client read patterns
  - forced client disconnect / cancellation
  - concurrency control and request pacing

3) Fault injection interface
- Supported injection modes:
  - In-process: runtime debug hooks/flags (preferred for determinism)
  - Sidecar: admin endpoint or local control socket
- Each injection is recorded as an event with timestamps.

4) Stall detector
- Evaluates forward-progress metrics and request liveness.
- Detects:
  - request-level hang (no tokens delivered, no completion/error)
  - TP-group-level stall (per-rank progress flatlines)
  - collective-level stall (collective latency spikes + missing completion events)

5) Artifact collector
- Structured run summary (JSON)
- Selected logs
- Optional: rank timeline trace markers

### Execution modes
- Local (developer)
  - Runs on a single multi-GPU node.
  - Outputs artifacts to a local directory.
- Benchmark lab (PR/perf validation)
  - Runs on curated GPU nodes.
  - Stores artifacts in centralized storage with run IDs.
- Perf-canary (nightly)
  - Runs scheduled scenarios; alerts on regressions in stall rates/watchdog triggers.

## Scenario design
Scenarios are defined as:
- Model + TP configuration
- Traffic pattern
- Fault injection plan
- Expected behavior + pass/fail thresholds

### Baseline configuration (common defaults)
- Model: a TP-enabled production-like model (selected per hardware tier).
- TP: 2 or 4 (depending on node).
- Streaming: enabled for at least one scenario.
- Continuous batching: enabled.
- Prefix/KV caching: enabled where supported.
- Max concurrency: tuned to reach ~80–95% GPU utilization (stress without immediate overload collapse).

### Traffic patterns (required set)
The suite must include the following traffic patterns, because they map to observed production hang signatures.

#### Pattern A: Mixed sequence lengths (fairness + barrier stress)
- Concurrency: 64–256 (scaled by GPU class)
- Requests:
  - 70% short (prompt 128–512 tokens, output 64–256)
  - 25% medium (prompt 1k–2k, output 512–1k)
  - 5% long (prompt 2k–8k, output 2k–8k)
- Scheduling mode: mixed queue with fairness enabled
- Purpose: exercise scheduler fairness/backpressure and barrier alignment under heterogeneous decode times.

#### Pattern B: Long-running streaming with client backpressure
- Concurrency: 32–128 streaming connections
- Client behavior:
  - reads slowly (sleep between chunks) OR pauses reads for N seconds
  - randomly disconnects 1–3% of streams per minute
- Purpose: reproduce cancellation/disconnect paths and ensure barriers do not deadlock when a request is canceled mid-step.

#### Pattern C: Overload step function (queueing + watchdog)
- Ramp: 0 → target concurrency over 60s
- Step: +50% concurrency for 120s
- Recovery: back to baseline for 120s
- Purpose: trigger overload handling, backpressure/load-shedding, and validate watchdog/quarantine does not create a “stuck group keeps receiving work” condition.

#### Pattern D: Bursty micro-batches (scheduler starvation check)
- Burst window: 10s burst / 20s idle
- Request mix: mostly short, with small fraction of medium
- Purpose: detect scheduler starvation or “stale barrier” behaviors when work arrives in bursts.

### Fault injection knobs (required set)
Fault injection is intentionally limited to mechanisms we can make deterministic and safe in test environments.

#### Injection 1: Rank delay / jitter
- What: introduce per-rank compute delay before/after a collective or at defined “decode step boundaries”.
- Params:
  - affected_rank: 0..tp-1 (or “random”)
  - delay_ms: e.g., 50–500ms
  - duration_s: e.g., 10–60s
  - jitter: optional (+/- X ms)
- Motivation: reproduces “one rank lags” cases that can cause barrier deadlocks if cancellation/error handling is wrong.

#### Injection 2: Forced request cancellation at boundary
- What: cancel a subset of in-flight streaming requests while they are:
  - waiting on a scheduler barrier
  - in the middle of a decode loop
  - between collective ops
- Params:
  - cancel_rate: 0.5–5% of requests per minute
  - cancel_alignment: “at_token_k”, “at_barrier”, or “random”
- Motivation: reproduces known deadlocks from disconnects/timeouts.

#### Injection 3: Collective timeout / async error surfacing test
- What: simulate a collective that exceeds a configured timeout threshold, then validate:
  - the async error is detected
  - the TP group is quarantined/aborted according to policy
  - requests fail fast with explicit error codes (no infinite hang)
- Params:
  - injected_collective: allreduce|allgather|reduce_scatter (as applicable)
  - exceed_timeout_by_ms
  - expected_policy: “quarantine”, “abort_group”, “retry_once_then_quarantine” (must match runtime config)
- Motivation: validates ADR-0147 behavior and prevents silent stalls.

#### Injection 4: Scheduler backpressure toggles
- What: run scenario variants with backpressure knobs changed (within safe ranges) to detect regressions.
- Params:
  - max_inflight_requests_per_tp_group
  - admission_control_mode
  - fairness_mode
- Motivation: tests that changes in scheduling/backpressure don’t reintroduce starvation or unbounded queues.

#### Injection 5 (optional, lab-only): GPU stream/event mis-order stress
- What: enable runtime debug mode that randomizes the order of certain non-functional stream/event operations (within correctness constraints).
- Motivation: catches cross-stream deadlock sensitivity. This is lab-only due to increased noise.

## Scenario configuration schema (v0)
Scenarios are defined in a single file and can be referenced by name.

Example (YAML):

name: tp_hang_repro_mixed_streaming_cancel
model: redwood-catalog://open/llm-xx
runtime_version: build_from_ci
hardware:
  gpus: 4
  tp: 4
  dtype: bf16
  quantization: none
traffic:
  mode: streaming
  concurrency: 96
  request_mix:
    short_pct: 0.70
    medium_pct: 0.25
    long_pct: 0.05
  client_read_behavior:
    slow_read_pct: 0.30
    pause_read_seconds: [0, 5]
faults:
  - type: cancel
    cancel_rate_per_min: 2.0
    alignment: at_barrier
  - type: rank_delay
    affected_rank: random
    delay_ms: 200
    duration_s: 30
pass_fail:
  max_stall_events: 0
  stall_threshold_s: 15
  max_watchdog_triggers: 0
  max_5xx_rate: 0.001
  max_timeout_rate: 0.001
artifacts:
  collect_logs: true
  collect_metrics: true
  collect_rank_progress: true
  output_dir: run_artifacts/

Notes:
- The runner expands request_mix into concrete prompts/targets using a seeded generator.
- “stall_threshold_s” should be aligned with runtime watchdog thresholds to avoid redundant/contradictory classification.

## Stall detection and verdict logic
The suite produces a single verdict per scenario: PASS / FAIL / FLAKY / INFRA_ERROR.

### Stall detection signals
The runner must consume (or derive) these signals:

1) Request liveness
- For every request: observe token events (streaming) or completion for non-streaming.
- If no token/completion/error is observed for > request_stall_threshold_s while the request is still considered in-flight → request stall event.

2) TP-group forward progress
- Use runtime metric: tp_rank_decode_steps_total{tp_group_id,rank}
- If all ranks in a TP group show no increase for > tp_group_stall_threshold_s while there are active requests assigned to that group → group stall event.

3) Collective health
- Use runtime metrics:
  - tp_collective_latency_ms_bucket{collective}
  - tp_collective_inflight{collective}
  - tp_collective_timeouts_total
- If collective inflight stays >0 and the same collective has no completion for > collective_stall_threshold_s → collective stall event.

4) Watchdog/quarantine
- Use runtime metrics/log events:
  - tp_group_watchdog_triggers_total
  - tp_group_quarantined_total
  - tp_group_resets_total
- A watchdog trigger is not automatically a test failure in all modes; it depends on the scenario’s expected_policy.

### Pass/fail criteria (default)
A scenario FAILs if any of the following occur:
- Any TP-group stall event (group-level) occurs.
- Any request stall event persists beyond stall_threshold_s.
- Timeout rate > max_timeout_rate.
- 5xx rate > max_5xx_rate.
- The runtime becomes non-responsive to health checks for > 30s.
- A watchdog trigger occurs in scenarios where expected triggers = 0.

A scenario is marked FLAKY if:
- It fails once but passes on retry, and the failure category is “INFRA_NOISE” (e.g., node eviction) or “NON-DETERMINISTIC_PERF” without a clear runtime stall signature.
- Flaky classification is only allowed in perf-canary/nightly; CI gating treats flakiness as failure until triaged and explicitly allowlisted.

### Success metrics (suite-level)
We track these at the suite level across runs:
- Hang reproduction rate (for known-bad builds) and elimination rate (for fixed builds).
- Mean time to detection (MTTD) for stall events.
- False positive rate (fails with no correlated runtime stall signatures).

## Test matrix
The suite supports a small, curated matrix. We intentionally avoid combinatorial explosion.

### Required hardware tiers (initial)
- 4x H100 (tp=4)
- 8x A100 (tp=4 or tp=8 depending on runtime support)

### Required runtime modes
- Hosted-like configuration (aggressive batching, streaming heavy)
- Dedicated-like configuration (more predictable throughput, stricter isolation)

### Required scenarios per tier
Minimum set per tier per night:
- Pattern A + Injection 1
- Pattern B + Injection 2
- Pattern C + Injection 3

PR gating set (reduced runtime):
- Pattern B + Injection 2 (short duration)
- Pattern A baseline (no faults) (sanity)

## Integration with CI
### When the suite runs
- Pre-merge (required for labeled changes)
  - Trigger conditions:
    - changes to runtime scheduler/TP lifecycle
    - changes to collective/error propagation
    - changes to watchdog/quarantine
    - changes to streaming cancellation path
  - Mechanism: GitHub label “runtime-tp-critical” OR path-based trigger in CI config.

- Post-merge (continuous)
  - Daily schedule on the benchmark lab.
  - Results posted to #eng-runtime and linked in the build summary.

### CI gating policy
- Pre-merge gating uses the reduced PR set.
- A single FAIL blocks merge.
- Allowlisting a failure requires:
  - linked incident/issue
  - documented rationale
  - time-bounded expiry (max 14 days)
  - owner assigned (Sofia Ivanova or Hiro Tanaka for runtime; Sahana Iyer for harness)

## Integration with perf-canary
### Nightly canary
- Runs full scenario set on each tier.
- Alerts on:
  - any group stall event
  - watchdog triggers above baseline
  - increase in timeout/5xx rates over trailing 7-day median

### Alert routing
- Primary: #eng-runtime-oncall (or current runtime oncall channel)
- Secondary: #eng-sre for widespread regressions

### Canary guardrails
- Perf-canary should run against:
  - latest release candidate runtime build
  - last known-good baseline build (A/B) at least 1 run per night
- If baseline also fails, treat as lab/infrastructure issue unless artifacts show a new signature.

## Required instrumentation (runtime)
The stress suite assumes the runtime exports the following metrics/events. If not present, the suite will mark the run as INFRA_ERROR (not PASS).

### Metrics (minimum)
- tp_rank_decode_steps_total{tp_group_id,rank}
- tp_group_active_requests{tp_group_id}
- tp_collective_latency_ms_bucket{collective,tp_group_id}
- tp_collective_timeouts_total{collective,tp_group_id}
- tp_group_watchdog_triggers_total{tp_group_id,reason}
- tp_group_quarantined_total{tp_group_id,reason}
- tp_group_resets_total{tp_group_id}
- request_cancellations_total{reason}
- http_5xx_total, http_timeouts_total (or equivalent API gateway counters)

### Structured logs (minimum)
- Event: TP_GROUP_QUARANTINED (fields: tp_group_id, reason, last_progress_ts, inflight_requests)
- Event: COLLECTIVE_STALL_SUSPECTED (fields: collective, inflight_ms, tp_group_id)
- Event: BARRIER_CANCEL_PATH (fields: request_id, tp_group_id, phase)

## Artifacts and reporting
Each scenario run produces:
- run_summary.json
  - build SHA, runtime version, node ID, GPU type, driver, TP, scenario name
  - verdict and failure category
  - key counters: stalls, watchdog triggers, resets, timeout/5xx rate
- metrics_snapshot.prom (or equivalent scrape dump)
- selected runtime logs (filtered by tp_group_id and scenario timestamps)
- optional: trace markers (if tracing is enabled in the environment)

The runner prints a concise “triage header” at the top of logs:
- Failure category suggestion: COMM_STALL | KERNEL_STALL | SCHEDULER_STARVATION | BARRIER_CANCEL_DEADLOCK | INFRA
- Top 3 suspect signals (e.g., “tp_collective_inflight stuck for allreduce”, “rank 2 decode steps flatlined”, etc.)

## Failure taxonomy (used in summaries)
- COMM_STALL
  - Collectives inflight, latency histogram tails explode, no progress.
- KERNEL_STALL
  - No collective inflight growth, but per-rank progress halts; GPU util may remain high or drop depending on stall.
- BARRIER_CANCEL_DEADLOCK
  - High cancellation rate; progress stops at barrier/cancel boundary; logs show repeated barrier wait entries.
- SCHEDULER_STARVATION
  - Requests queued, groups idle or partially active; fairness/backpressure configuration suspect.
- WATCHDOG_FALSE_POSITIVE
  - Watchdog triggers but progress resumes quickly and no request stalls; requires threshold tuning.
- INFRA
  - Node eviction, driver reset, unrelated network outage, storage failure.

## Operational considerations
### Runtime flags and safety
- Fault injection requires explicit enablement (e.g., RUNTIME_ENABLE_FAULT_INJECTION=1).
- Injection endpoints must only be available in non-production environments.

### Time budget
- PR gating target: <= 20 minutes total wall time.
- Nightly full suite target: <= 2 hours per hardware tier.

### Determinism guidelines
- Use fixed random seed per scenario.
- Use a fixed prompt corpus with stable tokenization.
- Log effective seed and prompt IDs used.

## Rollout plan
1) v0 (Week 1)
- Implement runner + two scenarios: Pattern A baseline, Pattern B + forced cancel.
- Integrate into benchmark lab (manual runs) and publish artifacts format.

2) v1 (Week 2–3)
- Add rank delay injection and stall detector using per-rank progress.
- Add CI reduced gating set behind label.

3) v2 (Week 4+)
- Add collective timeout injection aligned with ADR-0147 policy.
- Add perf-canary nightly runs + alerting and dashboard links.

## Ownership
- Harness and CI/perf-canary wiring: Sahana Iyer
- Scenario definitions and scheduler-focused cases: Marcus Reed (with Sofia Ivanova)
- Collective-focused cases and timeout/error policy alignment: Grace Kim / Yuki Sato (with Hiro Tanaka)
- Alerting thresholds and oncall usability: Rafael Mendes / Allison Grant

## Open questions
1) Which “model under test” is the default for each tier (H100 vs A100) to balance runtime realism vs execution time?
2) Should watchdog triggers be allowed (and expected) in specific fault scenarios, or should the suite always expect zero triggers and only explicit error propagation?
3) Do we need a lab-only scenario that runs TP=8 on 8x GPUs, or is TP=4 sufficient for initial coverage?

## Appendix: Default thresholds (initial proposal)
These defaults should be revisited after we collect 1–2 weeks of baseline canary data.

- request_stall_threshold_s: 20s
- tp_group_stall_threshold_s: 15s
- collective_stall_threshold_s: 10s
- max_timeout_rate: 0.1% per scenario
- max_5xx_rate: 0.1% per scenario
- expected_watchdog_triggers:
  - baseline scenarios: 0
  - fault scenarios:
    - rank delay: 0 (prefer scheduler robustness)
    - forced cancel: 0
    - collective timeout injection: 1+ allowed only if policy is “quarantine/abort” and requests fail fast

End of spec.
